headline: The Justice Department charged 17 Iranian hackers tied to the Mabna Institute even as password spraying surged 155-fold and data-theft crews battered public networks from Latvia to Texas.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers increasingly skip malware entirely and simply log in, as a 155-fold surge in password spraying and fresh credential dumps from Microsoft Entra tenants turn stolen logins into the fastest path past defenses.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Password Spraying and Credential Attacks Surge

emerging_trends.text: State-backed espionage stayed front and center as the Justice Department unsealed charges against Iran's Mabna Institute and researchers uncovered the SilkParasite campaign hitting Central Asian governments with five never-before-seen remote access tools.

Data-theft extortion kept widening its blast radius, with Clop parading more than 40 Windchill victims including Shell and Philips while cyberattacks knocked government and university networks offline from Latvia to Texas.

topics.title: Government and University Network Breaches
topics.latest_developments: Latvia's road-traffic agency confirmed thieves took data on roughly 1.2 million residents—about two-thirds of the population—drawing demands that senior officials resign; Berlin isolated its urban-development and mobility ministries from the government network after a breach; and the University of Texas at San Antonio delayed its fall semester three days to August 24, 2026 after weekend intrusions.
topics.summary: Attackers hit public institutions across three countries; UT San Antonio, serving more than 42,000 students under Senior Executive Vice President Andrea Marks, took phones and academic systems offline, and Berlin's precautionary cutoff has held since Friday.

sources.title: Latvian officials resign after cyberattack exposes data on 1.2 million people
Berlin cuts two state ministries off government network after security breach
University of Texas forced to take systems offline in San Antonio after cyberattack
Cyberattack forces UT San Antonio to delay start of fall semester

topics.title: Clop Names Windchill Victims
topics.latest_developments: Clop listed more than 40 victims of its PTC Windchill and FlexPLM data-theft campaign, naming Shell, Philips, Fiserv, Zebra, Mindray, and Largan Precision on its leak site.
topics.summary: Clop exploited a critical flaw in PTC's product-lifecycle-management software and planted a custom JavaServer Pages web shell built to decrypt stored credentials and map engineering data, then moved to extort the manufacturers it breached.

sources.title: Cl0p Ransomware Group Names Over 40 Victims of PTC Windchill Campaign
Clop-Linked Windchill Web Shell Decrypts Credentials and Maps Engineering Data
Clop created custom web shell for Windchill data theft attacks

topics.title: Iranian Mabna Institute Indictment
topics.latest_developments: The Justice Department charged 17 members of Iran's Mabna Institute with breaching email accounts at US government agencies and stealing intellectual property from dozens of universities, and the State Department offered rewards up to $10 million for information on five of the defendants.
topics.summary: The indicted hackers, tied to the Iranian government, targeted hundreds of universities and organizations in the United States and abroad; the Rewards for Justice program will pay for information leading to five named suspects.

sources.title: US charges Iranians for sprawling hacking campaign on government agencies, universities
US Charges 17 Iranian Hackers, Offers $10 Million Rewards for 5 of Them

topics.title: Password Spraying and Credential Attacks Surge
topics.latest_developments: Huntress measured a 155-fold jump in password-spraying attacks in the first half of 2026, including one campaign that fired more than 81 million login attempts in two weeks, while Palo Alto's Unit 42 updated its guidance after an actor calling itself TheHatman claimed a large haul of credentials from organizations' Microsoft Entra tenants.
topics.summary: The attacks exploit legacy authentication and login flows that bypass multifactor authentication; defenders should disable legacy protocols and close gaps that leave some sign-ins unprotected.

sources.title: Password spraying attacks surge 155x as hackers exploit MFA gaps
Threat Brief: Mitigating Large-Scale Credential Attacks (Updated August 18)

topics.title: SilkParasite Espionage in Central Asia
topics.latest_developments: Researchers exposed SilkParasite, a previously unreported espionage operation striking government bodies across Central Asia with seven remote-access-tool families, five of them never documented before: DriveSilkRAT, CookiETagRAT, NomadRAT, GoginRAT, and NodeEdgeRAT.
topics.summary: First spotted in late 2025, the intrusion set steals from Central Asian government agencies using an unusually broad custom toolkit.

sources.title: SilkParasite Espionage Campaign Targets Central Asian Governments with Five New RATs

topics.title: Operation CameraSwarm Hijacks Dahua Devices
topics.latest_developments: Hunt.io reconstructed Operation CameraSwarm from a 407-megabyte exposed working directory, finding attackers compromised more than 14,530 Dahua devices between June 17 and July 22, 2026 using credential attacks, two authentication-bypass flaws, and a peer-to-peer relay technique.
topics.summary: The campaign hijacked Dahua surveillance cameras and recorders at scale; owners should replace default credentials and patch the exploited authentication bypasses.

sources.title: Hackers Compromised 14,500+ Dahua Devices Using Credential Attacks, Auth Bypasses, and P2P

business_politics.title: Treasury Doubles Debt Buybacks to Arrest Bond Rout
business_politics.latest_developments: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved August 19 to double the department's buybacks of long-term government debt, and 30-year yields dove on the news even as officials said they will not use repurchases to calm acute market stress.
business_politics.summary: The selloff that began with the August 13 U.S. 30-year auction had driven long-term borrowing costs to multi-decade highs worldwide, and the Treasury's step to double repurchases pulled yields back for now; the intervention matters to every leveraged holder of duration, and some Wall Street desks warn the rout has further to run.

sources.title: US Treasury to double buybacks of long-term government debt
Stock Market Today: Bond Yields Dive After Bessent Steps Up Buybacks
Why Wall Street Thinks the Brutal Bond Rout Is Just Getting Started

business_politics.title: Iran Standoff Keeps the Strait of Hormuz Choked
business_politics.latest_developments: Oil rose a fourth straight day August 19 as talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the war stalled, and France moved to expel two Iranian officials after accusing Tehran of attacking French diplomats.
business_politics.summary: The U.S. blockade of Iranian ships has throttled traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint for much of the world's seaborne oil, keeping crude bid; France's expulsion of two Iranian officials widens a confrontation that has already drawn threats of Iranian strikes on American and European targets.

sources.title: Oil Rises on Persistent Hormuz Uncertainty
France to expel two Iranian officials in diplomatic row

business.title: Kennywood Hiring 300 for Phantom Fall Fest
business.latest_developments: Kennywood opened a job fair August 19 to fill more than 300 seasonal positions, including scare actors and makeup artists, before its Phantom Fall Fest opens.
business.summary: The West Mifflin amusement park Kennywood is recruiting scare actors, makeup artists, and other seasonal staff to run Phantom Fall Fest, its autumn Halloween event.

sources.title: Kennywood holding job fair ahead of Phantom Fall Fest, looking to fill 300 positions

business.title: Okane Opens Three-Level Sushi Spot Downtown
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Magazine reported August 19 that Okane, at 245 Fourth Avenue Downtown, runs three distinct dining experiences across its three floors.
business.summary: Okane occupies a three-story building at 245 Fourth Avenue in Downtown Pittsburgh; its ground-floor Sweet Spot pours Vietnamese coffee and fruit teas and plates desserts such as a fish-shaped matcha taiyaki, with sushi service upstairs.

sources.title: Dig in With Graver: Rooftop Sushi, Supermarket Smashburgers and a Coffee Cruiser

around_town.title: Sharpsburg Library Ends Its Food Pantry
around_town.latest_developments: The Sharpsburg Community Library will close its five-year emergency food pantry to concentrate on what it calls a bigger need for toiletries.
around_town.summary: The Sharpsburg Community Library ran an emergency food pantry for five years and now plans to redirect that effort toward supplying toiletries to residents.

sources.title: Sharpsburg Community Library ends food pantry to 'focus on bigger need for toiletries'

around_town.title: Deer Lakes Opens Year With New Leadership
around_town.latest_developments: The Deer Lakes School District starts the 2026 school year with new leadership and 10 newly hired teachers.
around_town.summary: The Deer Lakes School District in the Allegheny Valley begins the academic year under a new administration, adding 10 teachers to its ranks.

sources.title: Deer Lakes starts school year with new leadership and 10 new teachers

events.title: Pittsburgh's Inaugural Cat Walk
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper reported August 19 that the inaugural Cat Walk will center on Legion Memorial Park, pairing the walking tour with craft vendors and community tables.
events.summary: Pittsburgh holds its first Cat Walk on Saturday, August 22, in the Brighton Heights neighborhood, combining a walking tour with craft vendors and organizations tabling at Legion Memorial Park.

sources.title: Pittsburgh's inaugural Cat Walk will bring whiskers and "whimsy" to Brighton Heights this weekend

around_teams.title: Fittipaldo Fields Watt and Porter Contract Questions
around_teams.latest_developments: In his August 19 chat, Post-Gazette Steelers writer Ray Fittipaldo took reader questions on Aaron Rodgers, head coach Mike McCarthy, T.J. Watt, and cornerback Joey Porter Jr.'s contract.
around_teams.summary: Post-Gazette Steelers writer Ray Fittipaldo held his weekly chat August 19, working through the quarterback picture under new coach Mike McCarthy and questions about T.J. Watt and Joey Porter Jr.'s contract situation.

around_teams.title: Off The Bat Weighs the Pirates' Slide
around_teams.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette Off The Bat column asked whether the Pirates can still learn from their 2024 second-half collapse as this year's fade deepens.
around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette's Off The Bat column drew a line between the Pirates' current downturn and the team's 2024 collapse, questioning whether Pittsburgh can change course before the season slips away.

sources.title: Off The Bat: Is it too late for the Pirates to learn from the 2024 collapse?

team_usa.title: Moultrie Out for the Season With ACL Tear
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported August 18 that Portland Thorns and United States forward Olivia Moultrie will miss the rest of the NWSL season with a torn ACL.
team_usa.summary: Olivia Moultrie, the young United States women's national team forward, tore her ACL and will sit out the remainder of the NWSL season, though her Portland Thorns keep climbing ESPN's power rankings in her absence.

sources.title: Power Rankings: Even without Moultrie, Portland is on the rise as K.C. sinks
